findings.title: Global cleanup service interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: In `CleanUpService.Run`, the ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This runs all background cleanup jobs (temp files, expired snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, user invites, short URLs, and query history) every minute instead of every 10 minutes, while each cleanup cycle still has a 9-minute timeout (`const timeout = 9 * time.Minute` on line 89). This appears to be a leftover local debugging change and will significantly increase background database and filesystem load in production.

findings.title: Leftover Error-level debug logging in CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags
findings.body: In `CleanAnnotations` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 576, 579), `r.log.Error` is called unconditionally on every batch iteration, even when `err == nil`, and dumps the entire slice of `ids` (which can contain tens of thousands of IDs per batch) along with the SQL condition. Because cleanup runs periodically in the background, this will flood production error logs with large payloads on every cleanup cycle even when no errors occur and no annotations are deleted.

findings.title: Quadratic string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE IN clause
findings.body: In `deleteByIDs`, when running on SQLite with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, the `IN` list is constructed in a loop using `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` (lines 609-612). Because strings in Go are immutable, this copies the entire accumulated string on every iteration, resulting in O(N^2) allocations and time complexity over the batch size (e.g., 32,767 IDs in the added test case). Using a `strings.Builder` or `strconv.AppendInt` (as done in `getAccessControlFilter` at lines 387-395) avoids the quadratic allocations.

findings.title: Parameter limit check in deleteByIDs only handles SQLite and checks config instead of len(ids)
findings.body: `deleteByIDs` checks `r.db.GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite && r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit` before falling back to an parameterized `IN (?, ?, ...)` query. However, PostgreSQL and MySQL also enforce a maximum number of bind parameters per prepared statement (65,535 in both PostgreSQL's extended query protocol and MySQL). If `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` is configured above 65,535 (or `len(ids)` exceeds the limit), `deleteByIDs` will fail on PostgreSQL and MySQL when preparing the `DELETE` statement.
